frequency_question: How often is an incremental cash reserve ratio or equivalent temporary secondary reserve requirement enacted during periods of significant banking system liquidity surplus?
membership_rule: Members are central bank policy announcements introducing temporary marginal reserve requirements on deposit growth above a baseline date, excluding standard permanent reserve ratio changes.
window: Any comparable 4-month policy evaluation window following a surge in systemic liquidity.

cases.name: RBI incremental CRR historical equivalent (past guidance periods)

provenance_note: 2 cases named, 4 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.0x)
coverage_note: 2 named primary historical precedents for this exact instrument; believed to represent a broader class of about 4 distinct liquidity-surplus episodes requiring marginal reserve tools.
known_gaps: Geographic concentration primarily on the Reserve Bank of India's historical toolkit for unexpected liquidity surges.
skeleton: Central bank liquidity management episodes with high surplus liquidity where extraordinary ratios were considered: 4 distinct tightening cycles across emerging market central banks facing capital influxes, observed over 20 years, multiplied by the fraction of times an incremental ratio tool was preferred over standard open market operations.
multiplier: 4 major surplus episodes where secondary reserve tools were plausible, with 2 actual implementations of an iCRR-specific mechanism.
validity_reason: Central bank operational frameworks for liquidity management evolve slowly over decades.
